F_G14R_jOHA.transcript_text: As markets adjust to economic uncertainty, Bitcoin is quietly reentering the safe haven conversation. A potential hedge against a very specific kind of uncertainty. Let's unpack this a little. Periods of instability are rarely just about economics. They're often a sign that systems are being tested, that confidence is shifting, and that the status quo might not be as stable as it once seemed. And markets don't always like that. For currencies, this matters because when confidence shifts, it can impact exchange rates, inflation, and broader monetary stability. And when that happens, the question becomes which assets are recognized globally, which assets can preserve value across borders, and which assets are more resilient to systemic change. [music] Historically, people have turned to assets such as gold, but now for a growing number of people and institutions, Bitcoin is [music] part of that mental model. Bitcoin is not a hedge in the traditional sense. It's volatile and it isn't issued or guaranteed by any government, [music] but that might be precisely the point. It doesn't need a central bank and it isn't tied to anyone system. It doesn't rely on policy decisions. Bitcoin is scarce, borderless, [music] and neutral. There are only 21 million Bitcoin. That's it. [music] It's governed by math and consensus, not politics. It can be stored without a custodian, moved without a middleman, and accessed by anyone, anywhere. So when traditional systems come under pressure, whether inflation, policy shifts, or broader instability, Bitcoin starts to look less like a gamble and more like a hedge against systemic fragility. Now let's be clear, this doesn't mean that Bitcoin is a perfect shield. It's not a savings account and it won't perform predictably in every single scenario. But in a world where systems can shift quickly, Bitcoin offers a different kind of purpose, one rooted in decentralization. It's not without volatility, of course, but that can also be what makes it behave differently to traditional assets. And that difference is increasingly valuable. And over time, that's been reflected in performance. If we look at how much Bitcoin has outperformed gold over the last 10 years, the result is quite eye-opening. Since 2015, Bitcoin has achieved returns that far exceeds gold with growth measured in the tens of thousands of percent. Compared to gold's more modest, but still impressive gains, Bitcoin has still proved itself to be arguably one of the best performing assets of all time. So, there seems to be a shift, not just in how people invest, but also how they think about storing value. And in that conversation, Bitcoin is no longer the outsider. It's not replacing fiat, but there is something to work alongside it. And [music] for some, it's becoming a strategic fallback, a decentralized hedge in a centralized world, a global asset for an increasingly complex system. You don't have to be a full Bitcoiner to see what's happening. You just have to pay attention. My name's Jessica and thank you for watching.
